title: Milošević Revokes Kosovo's Autonomy — March Constitutional Amendments
note: Serbian Assembly voted March 28 1989 to strip Kosovo autonomy; provincial assembly coerced into accepting on March 23. Year and facts correct.

title: Trepča Miners' Strike and Crackdown on Albanian Protests
note: Strike began February 20 1989 underground at Trepča; state of emergency imposed; mass dismissals followed. Year and facts correct.

title: Kosovo Assembly Dissolved After Declaration of Sovereignty
note: Albanian deputies declared sovereignty July 2 1990; Serbian assembly dissolved Kosovo assembly July 5 1990. Year and facts correct.

title: Democratic League of Kosovo (LDK) Founded Under Ibrahim Rugova
note: LDK was founded December 23 1989, not 1990. Year is off by one — marked FALSE per rules.

title: Albanians Pushed Out of State Schools, Hospitals, and Workplaces
note: Mass dismissals of Albanian public-sector workers and parallel institution creation are well-documented from 1990-1991. Year consistent with sources.

title: Underground Albanian Referendum Endorses Independence
note: Clandestine referendum held September 26-30 1991; ~87% turnout among Albanians; 99% voted for independence. Only Albania recognised. Year and facts correct.

title: Rugova Elected President of Self-Declared Republic of Kosovo
note: Rugova elected president May 24 1992; Bujar Bukoshi served as PM (appointed October 1991, operated from Germany). Year and facts correct.

title: Kosovo Excluded from Dayton Peace Agreement
note: Dayton Accords November 1995 did not address Kosovo status; widely documented as a turning point undermining Rugova's nonviolent strategy. Year and facts correct.

title: Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) Emerges with First Attacks
note: KLA claimed first attacks in 1996; arms from Albanian collapse in 1997 expanded capacity. Year and facts correct.

title: Education Agreement Between Milošević and Rugova
note: US-mediated education normalisation agreement signed 1996; implementation collapsed. Year and facts correct.

title: Albanian State Collapse Floods Kosovo with Weapons
note: Albanian pyramid scheme crisis early 1997 led to arms depot looting; weapons flowed into Kosovo and boosted KLA. Year and facts correct.

title: Drenica Massacres Open Full-Scale Kosovo War
note: Attack on Jashari compound Prekaz March 5-7 1998 killed ~58 Albanians including 18 women and 10 children. Described as start of Kosovo War. Year and facts correct.

title: UN Security Council Resolution 1199 Demands Ceasefire
note: UNSC Resolution 1199 adopted September 23 1998 under Chapter VII. Year and facts correct.

title: Holbrooke-Milošević Agreement and OSCE Verification Mission
note: Holbrooke brokered October 1998 deal; 2,000-strong KVM deployed. Implementation patchy; fighting resumed. Year and facts correct.

title: Račak Massacre Triggers International Crisis
note: Massacre January 15 1999; 45 bodies found January 16 by OSCE; Walker publicly attributed to Serbian forces. Year and facts correct.

title: Rambouillet Talks Collapse
note: Talks February-March 1999 in Rambouillet; Belgrade rejected NATO deployment; Albanians eventually signed. Preceded bombing. Year and facts correct.

title: NATO Operation Allied Force — 78-Day Bombing Campaign
note: Campaign started March 24 1999, lasted exactly 78 days, ended June 10 1999. Year and facts correct.

title: Mass Expulsion of Kosovo Albanians During Bombing
note: ~850,000 Albanians expelled to Albania, North Macedonia, Montenegro during bombing. Year and facts correct.

title: Kumanovo Agreement and UNSC Resolution 1244
note: Kumanovo Military-Technical Agreement signed June 9 1999; UNSC Resolution 1244 adopted June 10 1999. Year and facts correct.

title: UNMIK and KFOR Deploy to Kosovo
note: KFOR entered June 12 1999 with ~50,000 troops; UNMIK assumed civilian governance. Year and facts correct.

title: Mass Return of Albanian Refugees and Serb Exodus
note: Hundreds of thousands of Albanians returned within weeks; 200,000-250,000 Serbs and Roma fled. Year and facts correct.

title: First Post-War Municipal Elections Won by LDK
note: Municipal elections October 2000 under UNMIK; LDK won majority; PDK second; Serbs boycotted. Year and facts correct.

title: Constitutional Framework for Provisional Self-Government Adopted
note: UNMIK promulgated Constitutional Framework May 2001 establishing PISG with Assembly, Government, President. Year and facts correct.

title: First General Elections to Kosovo Assembly
note: First province-wide assembly elections November 2001; LDK plurality; Rugova elected president early 2002. Year and facts correct.

title: Vienna Direct Dialogue Begins Between Pristina and Belgrade
note: UNMIK launched standards-before-status policy and first direct technical talks October 2003 in Vienna. Year and facts correct.

title: March Riots — Anti-Serb Violence Across Kosovo
note: March 17-18 2004 riots; 19 dead (8 Serbs, 11 Albanians); 4,100+ Serbs displaced; ~35-36 Orthodox sites damaged/destroyed; 900+ homes burned. Year and facts correct.

title: Kai Eide Report and Launch of Final Status Talks
note: Kai Eide UN report 2005 concluded status talks could no longer wait; Ahtisaari appointed November 2005. Year and facts correct.

title: Death of President Ibrahim Rugova
note: Rugova died January 21 2006 of lung cancer. Funeral drew massive crowds. Year and facts correct.

title: Ahtisaari Plan Proposes Supervised Independence
note: Ahtisaari presented Comprehensive Proposal March 2007 recommending supervised independence; Russia blocked UNSC adoption. Year and facts correct.

title: Hashim Thaçi's PDK Wins Parliamentary Elections
note: November 2007 elections; PDK won; Thaçi formed coalition. Year and facts correct.

title: Kosovo Declares Independence — February 17
note: Declaration adopted February 17 2008 by 109 of 120 assembly members (not unanimous — 11 Serb deputies boycotted). Description says 'unanimously' which is slightly inaccurate but not materially wrong about the year or core event.

title: Kosovo Constitution Enters into Force
note: Constitution entered into force June 15 2008 establishing parliamentary republic. Year and facts correct.

title: EULEX Rule of Law Mission Deployed
note: EULEX began operations December 9 2008; largest EU civilian CSDP mission. Year and facts correct.

title: ICJ Advisory Opinion on Independence Declaration
note: ICJ issued advisory opinion July 22 2010; 10-4 vote finding declaration did not violate international law. Year and facts correct.

title: First Post-Independence Elections After Government Collapse
note: Early elections December 2010 after constitutional court ruled Sejdiu violated constitution; PDK won; fraud allegations. Year and facts correct.

title: EU-Mediated Belgrade-Pristina Dialogue Begins
note: EU-mediated technical dialogue launched March 2011. Year and facts correct.

title: Northern Kosovo Border Crisis
note: July 2011 Pristina attempt to deploy customs officers at northern crossings; Kosovo police officer killed; KFOR took over gates. Year and facts correct.

title: End of Supervised Independence
note: International Steering Group declared end of supervised independence September 2012; ICO closed. Year and facts correct.

title: Brussels Agreement on Normalization of Relations
note: First Agreement of Principles signed April 19 2013 (not 'April 2013' generally — date confirmed). Thaçi and Dačić signed. Year and facts correct.

title: First All-Kosovo Local Elections Including Northern Municipalities
note: November 2013 local elections included four northern municipalities; Serbian List dominated Serb-majority areas. Year and facts correct.

title: Five-Month Government Formation Deadlock
note: June 2014 elections inconclusive; PDK-LDK grand coalition under Isa Mustafa formed December 2014. Year and facts correct.

title: Specialist Chambers and Specialist Prosecutor's Office Established
note: Assembly approved constitutional amendments August 3 2015 (Amendment 24) establishing KSC/SPO; tied to 2010-2011 CoE organ trafficking report. Year and facts correct.

title: Tear Gas in Parliament Over Brussels Agreements
note: Vetëvendosje released tear gas in assembly chamber late 2015 and into 2016 to block ASM ratification and Montenegro demarcation. Year and facts correct.

title: Ramush Haradinaj Returns as Prime Minister
note: Snap elections June 11 2017; Haradinaj elected PM September 9 2017 with coalition. Year and facts correct.

title: Border Demarcation with Montenegro Ratified
note: Event is dated 2017 but assembly ratified the agreement March 21 2018. Year is off by one — marked FALSE per rules.

title: Land Swap Proposal Floated and Rejected
note: Land swap/border correction discussions between Thaçi and Vučić in 2018-2019; Germany opposed; idea died. Year and facts correct.

title: Kosovo Imposes 100% Tariffs on Serbian and Bosnian Goods
note: Initial 10% tariff November 6 2018; escalated to 100% November 21 2018 after Kosovo's Interpol bid blocked. Year and facts correct.

title: Albania Earthquake Causes Cross-Border Damage in Kosovo
note: Magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near Durrës November 26 2019; 51 deaths; Kosovo sent rescue teams; two Kosovar citizens among victims. Year and facts correct.

title: Vetëvendosje Wins Snap Elections — Kurti's First Government
note: Vetëvendosje won October 2019 snap elections; Kurti formed LDK coalition February 2020; no-confidence vote March 25 2020. Event year assigned 2020 reflects government formation/collapse. Facts correct.

title: Washington Economic Normalization Agreement
note: Kosovo PM Hoti and Serbian President Vučić signed at White House September 4 2020. Kosovo-Israel mutual recognition included. Year and facts correct.

title: Hashim Thaçi Indicted and Resigns as President
note: Indictment confirmed November 2020; Thaçi resigned and transferred to The Hague. Trial began; verdict not yet issued. Year and facts correct.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic and Health System Strain
note: COVID-19 reached Kosovo March 2020; contributed to government collapse; ~5% GDP contraction. Year and facts correct.

title: Vetëvendosje Landslide Returns Kurti to Power
note: February 14 2021 landslide (~50% vote); Vjosa Osmani elected president April 4 2021. Year and facts correct.

title: License Plate Crisis at Northern Border Crossings
note: Reciprocal license plate measures September 2021 triggered Serb protests at Jarinje/Bërnjak crossings; KFOR helicopters deployed; EU mediated. Year and facts correct.

title: Northern Mass Resignations and License Plate Standoff
note: Kosovo Serb mass resignations from police, judiciary, institutions November 2022 over plate re-registration; barricades; EU/US mediation. Year and facts correct.

title: Kosovo Formally Applies for EU Membership
note: Application submitted December 14-15 2022; last Western Balkans state to apply; blocked by five non-recognising EU members. Year and facts correct.

title: Ohrid Implementation Annex Agreed but Not Signed
note: Verbal acceptance of implementation annex March 18 2023 in Ohrid; neither leader signed; Vučić later qualified commitments. Year and facts correct.

title: Northern Mayor Crisis and KFOR Soldiers Injured
note: Albanian mayors installed May 26 2023 in four northern municipalities; violent protests May 29 2023; 25 KFOR soldiers injured (11 Italian, 19 Hungarian — with some overlap; ~30 figure in event description is slightly low but within range). Year and facts correct.

title: Banjska Monastery Attack Kills Kosovo Police Officer
note: Armed ambush September 24 2023; Sergeant Afrim Bunjaku killed; attackers barricaded in Banjska monastery; 3 militants killed; Milan Radoičić admitted organising attack. Year and facts correct.

title: Council of Europe Parliamentary Assembly Recommends Kosovo Membership
note: PACE voted April 2023 to recommend Kosovo admission. Year and facts correct.

title: Dinar Ban in Northern Kosovo
note: Central Bank announced late 2023 with effect February 2024; Serbian dinar banned; salary/pension payments disrupted. Year and facts correct.

title: EU Visa Liberalization Takes Effect
note: Visa-free travel to Schengen for Kosovo passport holders effective January 1 2024; last Western Balkans state. Year and facts correct.

title: Closure of Serbia-Run Parallel Institutions in Northern Kosovo
note: Kosovo authorities closed Serbian parallel municipal offices and services in north in 2024; Western mediators concerned; Brussels dialogue frozen. Year and facts correct.

title: Ibar-Lepenac Canal Sabotage
note: Explosion November 29 2024 (not 'November 29 2024' as described — event says November 29, Wikipedia confirms same date). ~20kg TNT; water supply to power plants disrupted; arrests made. Year and facts correct.

title: Serbian List Boycott of Kosovo Institutions Persists
note: Serbian List boycott of Kosovo central institutions from November 2022 resignations continued through 2024; reserved seats unfilled. Year and facts correct.

title: Inconclusive February Elections and Government Deadlock
note: Elections February 9 2025; Vetëvendosje won 48 seats (of 120); no majority; all opposition parties refused coalition; snap elections held December 28 2025. Year and facts correct.

title: EU Lifts Punitive Measures on Kosovo
note: EU began phasing out punitive measures during 2025 following 2023 northern crisis. Year and facts correct.

title: Trial of Hashim Thaçi Continues at Specialist Chambers
note: Trial ongoing through 2025; prosecution demanded 45 years February 2026; verdict expected 2026+. Year and facts correct.

title: Diaspora Remittances Reach Record Share of GDP
note: Kosovo diaspora remittances consistently among highest in Europe as share of GDP; 15-17% figure consistent with World Bank data trends. Year and facts correct.

title: Continued Stalemate on Association of Serb Municipalities
note: ASM undelivered through 2025 despite repeated EU/US pressure; core dispute anchor. Year and facts correct.
